tldr: TOOLMAKER is an agentic framework that autonomously transforms scientific papers with associated code repositories into LLM-compatible tools, achieving 80% task correctness and substantially outperforming current state-of-the-art software engineering agents.
contributions: A novel agentic framework (TOOLMAKER) that autonomously converts existing scientific code repositories into LLM-compatible tools
A closed-loop self-correction mechanism for autonomous debugging during tool generation
TM-BENCH, a benchmark of 15 complex computational tasks across medical and non-medical domains with over 100 unit tests
methods: TOOLMAKER takes a GitHub URL and task description as input and operates in two stages: environment setup and tool implementation. During environment setup, an INSTALL_REPOSITORY agent clones the repository, reads documentation, and installs dependencies inside a Docker container, recording all write actions as a reproducible snapshot. In the implementation stage, an EXPLORE agent gathers information, a PLAN LLM call creates a step-by-step plan, and an IMPLEMENT LLM call generates candidate Python code. The framework then enters a closed-loop self-improvement loop: the candidate tool is executed, assessed by an LLM, and if failures occur, a DIAGNOSE_ERROR agent identifies root causes and REIMPLEMENT revises the code, with summaries of each iteration appended to the conversation history.
results: TOOLMAKER correctly implements 80% of the 15 benchmark tasks on TM-BENCH, substantially outperforming current state-of-the-art software engineering agents. On individual tasks from the table: Pathology conch_extract_features achieved 3/3 task invocations passed and 9/9 tests passed at $0.35 cost; musk_extract_features achieved 3/3 invocations and 6/6 tests at $1.19 cost; pathfinder_verify_biomarker achieved 0/2 invocations but 4/6 tests at $0.61 cost. OpenHands was unable to complete some tasks (e.g., musk_extract_features marked with ✗).
limitations: The benchmark contains only 15 tasks, which limits the breadth of evaluation. Some tasks had incomplete success (e.g., pathfinder_verify_biomarker passed 0/2 task invocations). The approach depends on the availability of public code repositories accompanying scientific papers, so it cannot be applied where code is not publicly shared. Tasks required manual pre-implementation verification to ensure they were well-defined and solvable.
